To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PARP inhibitors are most active in cancers deficient in BRCA1/BRCA2, that this is due to a failure of homologous reparation, that PARP inhibitors can also act as chemotherapy/radiotherapy sensitizers, and that this is likely to be due to the inhibition of non-homologous end joining.
the PARP inhibitor olaparib is a potent radiosensitizer in HR proficient cells and is a synthetic lethal agent for HR deficient cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of biomarkers that predict sensitivity and resistance to PARP inhibitors.
identifying biomarkers for the sensitivity of cancers to PARP inhibitors.
the development of predictive biomarkers for PARP inhibitor therapy, with the ultimate aim of improving the efficacy and safety of PARP inhibitors in cancer therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no reliable biomarkers of PARP sensitivity.
PARP inhibitors have shown efficacy in HR deficient cancers and are being developed for HR proficient cancers in combination with chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
PARP inhibitors are active in BRCA1/BRCA2 mutated cancer, and may also be effective in sporadic cancer, but the data are not yet sufficient to define the exact indications for PARP inhibitor therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PARP inhibitor activity in vitro and in vivo is dependent on both the PARP inhibitor used, and the DNA repair status of the cancer cell line.
PARP inhibitors are most likely to be effective in cancers with a high level of genomic instability and a high level of DNA damage.
we have developed a number of biomarkers for PARP inhibitor sensitivity and that we are now using these biomarkers to identify patients who are likely to respond to PARP inhibitor therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of PARP inhibitors in sporadic cancer is not as simple as using them in BRCA1/BRCA2 related cancer.
the PARP inhibitors have a spectrum of activity, and that the development of predictive biomarkers for PARP inhibitors is urgently required to ensure the success of future clinical trials.
the biomarkers for PARP inhibitor single agent sensitivity are different from those for chemotherapy sensitization.
